title: Largest XOR of any pair
prompt:
Return the largest value of a XOR b over every pair of values a and b taken from two different positions in the list.

- 2 to 100,000 integers with 0 <= value < 2^30. The bound keeps JavaScript bitwise operators, which work on 32-bit signed integers, safe.
- Values may repeat; a repeated value XOR itself is 0.
- Return a single integer. Aim for better than O(n²).
hints: XOR rewards high bits most. Decide the answer one bit at a time, starting from bit 29.
Suppose you already know the best top bits. Try setting the next bit too: the candidate is (best << 1) | 1 compared against prefixes v >> bit.
Put every prefix v >> bit in a set. The candidate is achievable if some prefix p has p ^ candidate in the set, because a ^ b = c means a ^ c = b. (A binary trie of the values works too.)

solution.explanation: A higher bit outweighs all lower bits combined, so the answer can be fixed greedily from bit 29 down. At each step the question is whether two prefixes XOR to the best-so-far with one more 1 appended, which a hash set answers in linear time using a ^ b = c ⇔ a ^ c = b. A prefix XOR-ed with itself gives 0, never the odd candidate, so a match always comes from two different positions.

complexity.notes: B = 30 is the number of bits, so this is linear in n for fixed-width values. A binary trie gives the same bound by walking each value toward the opposite bit.

followUps: Answer many queries: for each query x, return the largest x XOR v among values v <= limit.
